Subject: Dedicated capacity — packaging & throughput scenarios

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week. Anita and I mapped a couple of production constraints and want to understand sizing and commercial packaging for a Dedicated GPU pool. High level:
- Peak queries: ~1.8M requests/month (non-uniform, ~30% of traffic in a 3 hour evening window)
- Request profile: 20–60 tokens input on average, ~128 tokens output (mostly chat assistant)
- Client-side concurrency: expected 230 steady concurrent websocket sessions during peak; request bursts can hit 500 concurrent token-streams for short periods
- SLO: 95th percentile latency <200ms for token streaming; acceptable to have short bursts handled by burst capacity or fair-share policies

Can you propose a recommended GPU pool (instance mix, number of GPUs), an expected throughput guarantee, and the committed pricing tiers / discount philosophy? Also send any packaging limits (min commit term, overage rates, credits).

Appreciate a short table or scenarios we can review.

Carl
Director of AI Ops
LumenLabs

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — packaging & throughput scenarios

Hi Carl — thanks for the clear profile. We sketched three realistic packaging scenarios (conservative, baseline, and aggressive) based on your numbers and the expected traffic burstiness. See the short summary below — attaching the modeling workbook with assumptions.

Key modeling assumptions (from workbook):
- Average in/out tokens per request: 150 tokens total
- Average tokens/sec per GPU (quantized mix): 65 tokens/sec for generation-heavy chat models (fp16 4-bit-like throughput equivalent)
- Continuous concurrency factor: assume 80% of steady sessions are actively generating at any moment
- Burst handling: use 2x short-burst capacity (30-min smoothing window) with priority preemption and overage credits to keep latency SLOs

Scenarios (monthly commit):
- Conservative (lower risk)
  - Commit: 40 A100-equivalent GPUs
  - Modeled steady throughput: ~320k requests/day (peak headroom ~1.8x)
  - SLA-backed 95th latency target: 220ms (streaming optimized)
  - Pricing: list price 1.0x, 10% volume discount on overage applies

- Baseline (recommended for current profile)
  - Commit: 28 A100-equivalent GPUs
  - Modeled steady throughput: ~225k requests/day (burst headroom ~1.5x)
  - SLA-backed 95th latency target: 200ms
  - Pricing: 1-year commit, 15% committed-discount off list, 2 months free credits if signed by Sep 15

- Aggressive (cost-optimized)
  - Commit: 18 A100-equivalent GPUs + 6 T4-like low-cost GPUs for short-tail batches
  - Modeled steady throughput: ~160k requests/day (higher utilization, less headroom)
  - SLA-backed 95th latency target: 240ms with best-effort burst handling
  - Pricing: 20% off list, overage at 1.4x list rate, 12-month min term

Tradeoffs / notes:
- Baseline is our recommendation for balancing cost & headroom given your evening surge pattern.
- We model memory/KV cache pressure for context lengths up to 2,000 tokens; if you expect longer contexts we should add +20% GPU count for KV overhead.
- Canary & staggered rollouts: we can reserve a small canary slice (2–4 GPUs) in Dedicated for model testing at no additional commit for the first 30 days.

Attachments: RL-Dedicated-Packaging-Scenarios-v1.xlsx; Redwood_Dedicated_Commit_Tiers_v3.pdf

Action items: if you send expected growth (3–6 month), we’ll produce a final quote with formal commit terms and an overage credit proposal.

Best,
Mina Haddad

Thanks — that is very helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement / finance perspective:

- What flexibility do we have around the 1.5x burst headroom claim? If we cross sustained bursts for >2 hours is there an automatic fallback to Hosted (and what are those rates)?
- On discounts: the 15% with 2 months credits is a good start — can you provide a counter that includes an early-payment discount (net 30 -> additional 3%) and a milestone credit tied to latency SLOs?

Also, vendor security had one question: are Dedicated audit logs (per-request traces) exportable to our SIEM for 90 days? We need a note for procurement.

Carl

Hi Carl — quick commercial note from my side on options that help with procurement asks: 

1) 24-month Baseline variant (proposal):
- Base commit: 26 A100-equivalent GPUs (2 GPU reduction vs 1yr baseline)
- Pricing: 19% committed discount on list, milestone credits: up to 6% rebate if P95 latency <200ms and uptime >=99.8% across month
- Early-pay: additional 3% off invoice if net30 paid within 10 days (applies to committed portion)
- Overages: charged at 1.2x list for first 10% overage, 1.5x beyond 10%
- Flex: option to convert up to 10% of committed capacity to Hosted burst at negotiated rate (good for sustained >2hr events)

2) Canary + Audit export add-on:
- Canary (2 GPUs) free for first 30 days for validation; subsequent canary usage billed as committed if converted
- Audit logs: we can export per-request traces to your SIEM (S3 or Splunk HTTP ingest) for 90 days as an add-on. We’ll include it in the quote as a standard compliance pack for enterprise deals.

If this looks close, we can draft a 24-month term SOW and include a few SLA milestones that trigger the rebate.

Thanks,
